MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Male
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Clinical Indication: Diagnostic investigation for Cystic Fibrosis in setting of infertility. Suspected congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens.

TEST PERFORMED
CFTR Gene Targeted Sequencing Panel

METHODOLOGY
Targeted next-generation sequencing of the CFTR gene including exons 4, 6a, 7, 10-13, 19-21 and part of intron 19. This panel covers approximately 88% of pathogenic variants found in individuals of Caucasian ancestry, 56% in South Asian populations, and 76% of worldwide CF mutations. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. Library preparation was performed using amplicon-based enrichment followed by sequencing on an Illumina platform. Minimum coverage of 100x was achieved for all targeted regions. Variant calling and annotation were performed using a validated bioinformatics pipeline. Nomenclature follows HGVS guidelines using NM_000492.4 as the reference sequence.

RESULTS

CFTR (NM_000492.4):
1. c.1727G>C; p.(Gly576Ala) - Heterozygous
   Location: Exon 13
   Classification: Variant of uncertain significance
   Population frequency: 0.0002 (gnomAD v3.1.2)

2. c.2002C>T; p.(Arg668Cys) - Heterozygous
   Location: Exon 15
   Classification: Variant of uncertain significance
   Population frequency: 0.0001 (gnomAD v3.1.2)

3. Intron 8 PolyT tract: 7T/7T
   Classification: Normal variant

INTERPRETATION
Two heterozygous variants were identified in the CFTR gene: c.1727G>C (p.Gly576Ala) and c.2002C>T (p.Arg668Cys). Based on population frequency data and previous reports in the literature, these variants likely represent a complex mild allele in cis configuration (on the same chromosome) with variable penetrance. When present together on the same allele, these variants have been associated with CFTR-related disorders, particularly when paired with a severe pathogenic mutation on the opposite chromosome.

The 7T/7T genotype at the intron 8 polyT tract is considered normal and is not associated with reduced CFTR function.

These findings support but do not definitively confirm a diagnosis of CFTR-related disease. The patient's infertility may be related to CFTR dysfunction if congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD) is clinically confirmed. Individuals with mild CFTR variants in cis configuration may have variable clinical presentations ranging from asymptomatic to CFTR-related disorders including CBAVD, chronic pancreatitis, or bronchiectasis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Parental testing is recommended to confirm that the two variants are in cis configuration (on the same chromosome)
2. Carrier testing should be offered to the patient's partner prior to conception, as offspring would be at risk for cystic fibrosis if the partner carries a pathogenic CFTR variant
3. Genetic counseling is recommended for the patient and at-risk adult relatives
4. If congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens is clinically confirmed, consider extended CFTR mutation analysis to identify potential additional variants not covered by this panel
5. Clinical correlation with urological evaluation is recommended

LIMITATIONS
This test interrogates selected regions of the CFTR gene and does not detect all possible mutations. Deep intronic variants, large deletions/duplications, and variants in non-targeted exons would not be detected. This test has not been validated for detection of somatic mosaicism. Variant interpretation is based on current knowledge and may change over time as new information becomes available.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
